status: User approved visual family and narrow split; Flow requires statechart redesign; design only, no runner implemented
purpose: Observe the selected real runner state machine and its recorded execution history, including verification, waits, failures and durable decision delivery.

placement.panel: Separate optional, closable System panel in the native extra-panel list
placement.defaultScope: Routed session and its explicit plan/worker links
placement.broaderScope: Current canonical project only when explicitly selected
placement.layout: Narrow side panel: visualization above selected-run detail; full-width horizontal resizable divider; independent scrolling. Never a right-hand inspector column.
placement.appearance: Host UI font, reactive mono font, semantic theme tokens and native controls; image colors and type sizes are illustrative.

views.flow: Actual runner statechart for a selected run/attempt: definition states and transitions, active snapshot, recorded transition history and selectable reasons; Architect appears only at recorded decision boundaries. The dependency-flow image is visual family only and must be redesigned.
views.timeline: Compact task/attempt lanes sharing an observed time axis with recorded execution and verification spans, waits and decision events where available; selected detail below the timeline.
sharedInspector: Selected run, task and attempt or state/transition identity
Recorded failure or wait reason and evidence
Next decision and responsible actor when recorded
Outcome persistence and delivery state when recorded

principles: Flow uses the actual authoritative runtime machine definition and snapshot; XState adoption is a future choice and prerequisite to an XState-backed slice, not an existing integration. Task dependency edges are not state transitions.

The GUI reads versioned topology and persisted state/transition projections; it never starts a second actor, replays side effects, or sends historical events to a live actor. Guard labels alone do not prove a transition is enabled.
Runtime owns state transitions; visualizations observe durable facts, never infer acceptance from agent narration.
Architect is woken for decisions, not represented as a continuously running scheduler.
Show dependency, resource and scope waits only when recorded with causal references.
Render real machine, run and attempt identities, recorded transitions, timing and delivery from a consistent scoped snapshot/replay contract.
Use stable node/row placement, keyboard selection, reduced-motion support and preserved session scope/selection.
Report stale/disconnected snapshots honestly and resync after gaps; last known data is not current live evidence.
No completion-time forecast or invented percentage progress; generated bar positions and example timings are not an exact data specification.
Build after actual runner/attempt/outcome data exists, via an Architect-specified increment; no production mock telemetry.
